spoken: I was genuinely worried after Thursday's MRI scan on his left thigh. But Alcaraz walked out with that black bandage and swept past Flavio Cobolli 6-4, 6-1!
That makes it twelve straight wins for the Spaniard. He hit twenty-nine winners, gave Cobolli zero openings on serve, and completed a perfect group stage.
Three wins out of three! He also defeated Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 earlier in the week. Now it is Ben Shelton in Saturday's semi-final.
He needed a medical timeout against Medvedev, but his medical team cleared him to play. He kept the rallies short against Cobolli and looked fully fit.
Huge news for Real Madrid fans! Thibaut Courtois has signed a contract extension until June 2028!
The 34-year-old Belgian goalkeeper joined from Chelsea in 2018. He has 348 appearances, 133 clean sheets, three LaLiga titles, and two Champions League crowns.
Player of the match in that 2022 Champions League final victory over Liverpool, Yashin Trophy, Golden Glove in 2018... locking him down for two more years is incredible.
Also at Madrid, Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, and Lamine Yamal have been nominated for the 2026 Globe Soccer Awards.
And Vinicius Jr. is back in the squad for Sunday's game against Celta Vigo!

He missed four LaLiga matches following his red card against Villarreal. After scoring five goals in two games for Brazil during the international break, he returns alongside Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva. Real Madrid are second with 30 points from 12 matches, three points behind leader Barcelona.
In cricket, India A started their Rising Stars Asia Cup campaign in Doha with a brilliant hundred from Tilak Varma!

After Abhishek Sharma fell for nine and Ayush Badoni went early against Nepal, captain Tilak Varma made 107 off 113 balls. He added 206 runs for the fourth wicket with Kumar Kushagra, who scored 117. Tilak eventually fell caught on the boundary trying to hit Nandan Yadav over long-on.
And what about the first Test in Wellington? Glenn Phillips gave us a hard time on Day 2.

He did. Phillips reached his second Test hundred off 193 balls off Prasidh Krishna. He became the first batter to score a Test, ODI, and T20I hundred against India in a calendar year, building on his partnership with Henry Nicholls.
But Akash Deep got him in the end!

In his first Test after a 16-month absence with a lower-back stress fracture, Akash Deep knocked back the top of off stump. India ended Day 2 at 159 for one, with Jaiswal scoring 85 off 89 balls, trailing New Zealand by 209 runs.
Did you see Krishnamachari Srikkanth questioning how fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is being handled?
Srikkanth strongly criticised the selectors, saying playing him for one match and leaving him out for five is a blunder that discourages young talent.
Over in Formula 1, Max Verstappen had a messy opening day of practice in Las Vegas.

Wet weather limited FP1 with no lap times set. In FP2, Verstappen finished 13th, reporting car balance, handling, and power issues. Technical director Pierre Wache admitted Red Bull have work to do. Still, Max enters Vegas second in the standings after three wins in his past five races.
The Golden State Warriors are in absolute freefall without Steph Curry. Lost 116-94 to Dallas and 126-98 to Memphis.

They have dropped four straight on a winless road trip, falling to 8-7 in the last play-in spot. With Curry out due to an oblique tear, Will Richard scored 20 points off the bench against Dallas, going eight for eight on two-pointers while Cooper Flagg scored 33 for the Mavericks. Steve Kerr says they have to find a way to execute.
Look back at tennis history for a second—Novak Djokovic's epic five-set 2014 Wimbledon final victory over Roger Federer, 6-7, 6-4, 7-6, 5-7, 6-4.

That three-hour and 56-minute match denied Federer an eighth Wimbledon title and earned Djokovic his second. Off the court, Cristiano Ronaldo is co-funding a 22.4 million dollar bottled water plant in Gostei, Portugal, with Maravilha Decimal and Grupo Outeirinho, opening in late 2027.
What is the latest on Formula 1 stewards?

The FIA is recruiting 12 to 15 full-time stewards starting in 2027 to improve officiating consistency. Also, Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss confirmed Valtteri Bottas stays for 2027, keeping Colton Herta as test driver.

Around the grounds. UEFA hit England with a suspended one-match away supporter ban for two years after discriminatory anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting during their 3-2 win against Spain in Madrid.
And Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt on his birthday! The club posted a birthday wish on social media at 9.08am and announced his departure at 4pm!

spoken: Man, Carlos had me sweating! He lost the first set 3-6 against Ben Shelton, but clawed back 6-3, 7-6 with a 7-1 tiebreak in the semi-final!
Digging deep to reach the summit clash again in Turin. He now faces Alexander Zverev, after Zverev beat Medvedev 7-6, 6-4.
Those two actually played a practice set before the tournament that lasted over an hour and a half!
The undefeated champion takes home five point one seven million dollars. The runner-up gets two point seven five million. Alcaraz is also only the fourth Spaniard since 1998 to reach this final.
Now, Real Madrid! Down 0-1 at six minutes against Celta Vigo through Pablo Durán's goal from Williot Swedberg's assist. I was losing my head!
Five straight wins prior, but a poor first half at the Bernabeu.
But Jude Bellingham equalises in the sixty-sixth minute off a Kylian Mbappé assist, and Carlos Espí bags the winner in the eighty-fifth! Two-one victory! Espí said he got goosebumps!
Thibaut Courtois produced vital saves and credited Jose Mourinho's half-time team talk for turning the match around. Madrid also made a touching gesture before kickoff.
How does the table look now?
Barcelona stay top with thirty-three points. Real Madrid are second, also on thirty-three points. Atlético Madrid sit third with twenty-eight, and Real Betis are fourth on twenty-seven.
Rafa Nadal is officially on the Real Madrid board of directors now!

Indeed. Approved with ninety-nine point five percent of the member assembly votes—seventeen hundred and four out of seventeen hundred and thirteen. He walked in alongside Pirri to the anthem of La Décima. Florentino Pérez welcomed the twenty-two-time Grand Slam winner, noting the club hasn't won a trophy since 2024.
Plus, Pérez announced at the general assembly in Valdebebas that European football will stream for free in India starting next season on a new platform!
A UEFA pilot project to expand viewership, even as Sony Sports Network holds broadcast rights through 2026-27 under a forty-million-dollar deal.
Las Vegas Grand Prix! Max Verstappen started on grid P1 and took victory! Seventy-fifth career win!
An extraordinary race featuring thirty-five overtakes for the lead. Max held off George Russell, Lando Norris, and Kimi Antonelli.
His swoops around Russell through Turn Two were unbelievable! Driver of the Day!

Antonelli was actually fastest in qualifying by zero point two five eight seconds over Max, but took a five-place grid penalty for engine components. Russell started second, Norris third, and rookie Arvid Lindblad was promoted to sixth.
What about the incidents during the race?

Lap eighteen saw a Safety Car when Sergio Perez thudded into Rafael Camara's Haas at Turn Fourteen. Perez retired, while Camara continued. Lewis Hamilton took a ten-second penalty for passing Norris off-track. Isack Hadjar ran second but suffered a late front-wing collapse and got a post-race penalty for slowing down before double stacking.
And Max didn't hold back on Russell after the race!

He unleashed sharp comments following Russell's qualifying remarks. McLaren grabbed a double podium with Norris second and Oscar Piastri third. In the standings, Antonelli leads on four hundred and two points, Verstappen is second with three hundred and four, Hamilton third on two hundred and sixty-seven, with Russell and Norris tied on two hundred and sixty-four. Red Bull lead McLaren by nine points for third in the constructors.
Over in Wellington, India declared at a massive seven hundred and twenty for nine after New Zealand made three hundred and sixty-eight!
Yashasvi Jaiswal scored eighty-five, KL Rahul one hundred and thirty-six, Devdutt Padikkal eighty, Shubman Gill ninety-eight, and Dhruv Jurel seventy-eight.
But Rishabh Pant! A classic hundred off one hundred and thirty-five balls! A reverse sweep on ninety-nine, and a six off Glenn Phillips to reach his ninth Test century!
Pant now has one hundred and eight Test sixes, passing Brendon McCullum. He is the first visiting wicket-keeper to score Test hundreds in all SENA countries.
And Jasprit Bumrah! He bowled Tom Latham for a two-ball duck in the first innings, then got him for another duck off the second ball in the second innings!
Joining Zaheer Khan from 2007 and Sreesanth as the only Indian pacers to do that double in a Test.
Over in Doha at the Asia Cup Rising Stars, India A versus Pakistan A started with complete chaos at the toss!
The match referee initially announced the wrong result. Pakistan A captain Abdul Samad corrected him, and rechecking confirmed Pakistan A won the toss and chose to bat on a dry pitch.
Alexander Zverev cruised past Daniil Medvedev seven-six, six-four in the other ATP Finals semi-final.
Solid display, taking the first set tiebreak seven-nil.
Cristiano Ronaldo scored his nine hundred and eighty-sixth career goal, but Al Nassr fell three-one to Al Ahli!

Ronaldo opened the scoring at fourteen minutes but hit the post with a penalty four minutes later. Galeno equalized, then Ivan Toney converted a penalty and Roger Ibañez added a third. Merih Demiral was named player of the match. Al Nassr remain third on twenty-eight points, two behind Al Hilal.
Novak Djokovic is making a Hollywood cameo alongside Owen Wilson in the comedy Focker-In-Law!
Carrying a tennis bag and trading banter about forehands and backhands.
Ferrari had another disaster in Vegas! Charles Leclerc spun Lewis Hamilton!
Fred Vasseur was furious after their earlier clash in Mexico and their team meeting in Sao Paulo. Both cars exited Q2 in qualifying due to tyre warm-up struggles in the cold.
The Warriors are sliding fast without Steph Curry, dropping five straight road games.
Spurs, Celtics, and Grizzlies now lead the NBA in Net Rating.
And Isack Hadjar says he has no clue why his front wing snapped in Vegas, suspecting a big bump under braking into Turn Five.
In the Premier League, Chelsea were hammered four-one at home by Leeds United. A three-goal defeat on home soil.

spoken: What a night in Turin! Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev six-two, seven-six, taking the tiebreak nine-seven to capture his first ATP Finals trophy. I was on the edge of my seat!

He was relentless. Remember, faster indoor courts were supposed to be his weak spot. Not anymore. He goes undefeated all week, earns the maximum fifteen hundred points, and moves to seven thousand six hundred points overall.

He is only three hundred and fifty points behind Jannik Sinner now! Sinner is on seven thousand nine hundred and fifty points and has not played since Wimbledon while facing possible knee surgery. Zverev still finishes the year at number one with ten thousand three hundred and fifty.

Think about where Alcaraz started this year. He won the Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam as the youngest man ever, then missed four and a half months with that wrist injury. Now he joins Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, and Novak Djokovic as the fourth man to win all four majors and the season-ending finals.

And he proved all the doubters wrong after splitting with his longtime coach Juan Carlos Ferrero. Plus, he confirmed he will play the Davis Cup Final Eight in Bologna this week, a year after missing it with a hamstring issue.
He said withdrawing was never considered, even after that MRI scan following the Medvedev match. Now, from Turin joy to Wellington frustration.
Seven hundred and twenty for nine declared! Our highest Test score ever in New Zealand! How did we not win this Test match?

Because the Basin Reserve pitch turned completely flat. New Zealand made three hundred and sixty-eight in their first innings, and after India declared with that massive two hundred and thirty-three run lead, Devon Conway batted out of his skin with an unbeaten fifty. They reached two hundred and thirty-nine for five to hold on for a draw.

Our bowlers ran themselves into the ground! Nearly two hundred and fifty overs across two innings! Jasprit Bumrah bowled forty-nine overs for five wickets. Akash Deep bowled forty-three, Anshul Kamboj forty-five, and Prasidh Krishna forty-five, each getting three wickets.

Which is why captain Shubman Gill cancelled their planned team activity in Christchurch. He said the bowlers deserved a proper rest and promised to take them out for dinner instead. The two-match series stays zero-zero.
Gill was complaining about the Kookaburra ball getting soft far too early, asking why the ICC cannot bring back saliva to help shine the ball.

The ICC has made it clear they have no plans to review the saliva ban, which was made permanent after the pandemic. Meanwhile, Matthew Hayden has come out saying the old Sandpapergate talk will fade away as Australia shifts focus to the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

Also in cricket, India A made three changes for their Asia Cup Rising Stars match against UAE, who elected to bat. Prabhsimran Singh, Harsh Dubey, and Arshad Khan came in for Ayush Badoni, Vipraj Nigam, and Prince Yadav.
Over in Formula 1, Max Verstappen put on a masterclass in Las Vegas, winning from pole position.
Thirty-five lead changes in fifty laps! Max kept re-passing everyone down that long straight. Laurent Mekies said Max is from a different planet with how he outsmarted the grid!
Verstappen was not entirely thrilled though. He criticised the heavy slipstreaming, saying this is not real F1. And he had a sharp word for George Russell.

Russell talked big before the race, then crashed into the wall trying to pass his teammate Kimi Antonelli! Max literally said karma is a bitch and declared Russell is so far below his level. You have to love the brutal honesty!
Switching to football, Real Madrid have a bit of a squad headache ahead of European action.
Endrick is out for two to three weeks with a left leg abductor muscle injury! At least Denzel Dumfries avoided serious ankle damage and made the squad.

Thibaut Courtois came out in defense of Vinicius Junior, saying only Messi and Ronaldo sustain peak levels without criticism. Jose Mourinho also backed Vini, reminding everyone that his four-game suspension disrupted his rhythm.
The Warriors finally ended that painful five-game losing streak! They scraped past the Boston Celtics eighty-eight to eighty-seven at Chase Center.

That was pure grit. Missing Stephen Curry with his abdominal issue, plus Butler, Moody, Porzingis, and Brandon Williams, they held Jayson Tatum and Boston to eighty-seven points. Boston has now lost four straight.
And point guard Brandon Williams is set to return on Wednesday night against Sacramento! His pace will give our offense a massive lift.
In Shanghai, a massive seven-meter statue of Cristiano Ronaldo was unveiled outside a shopping center on East Nanjing Road to open his CR3000 square meter museum.
The tallest full-body statue of him in the world, doing the iconic Siu celebration! His brother Hugo was there, though Ronaldo himself missed it.
In F1 driver news, Haas confirmed rookie Rafael Camara will complete the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, ending his F2 title bid where he was leading by seven points.
And at Ferrari, questions are flying about whether Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc can keep working together after more on-track drama in Vegas.

Around the grounds. In the Premier League, Brentford thrashed ten-man Everton four-nil. Keane Lewis-Potter scored two deflected goals before James Tarkowski was sent off, spoiling David Moyes' record five hundred and ninety-third game in charge of Everton.
And in domestic T20 cricket, Priyansh Arya smashed a sensational one hundred and eighty-one, the second-highest individual score in T20 history!

spoken: Dhruv, I was genuinely sweating at half-time. Ivan Perisic puts PSV ahead from the penalty spot in the 32nd minute. But this Real Madrid side just hits another gear!

They certainly did. Federico Valverde levelled it in the 50th minute off an Arda Güler assist. Then Jude Bellingham produced a dazzling volley in the 60th from Kylian Mbappé's pass to put Madrid in front.
What a goal from Jude! That volley was unbelievable!

Mbappé then took over. He made it 3-1 in the 64th minute, again set up by Güler, added his second in the 84th off Brahim Díaz, and Vinícius Júnior wrapped up the 5-1 win from a Bellingham assist in the 87th.
That is five straight Champions League wins! Ten straight wins in all competitions across La Liga and Europe, scoring 31 goals and conceding just 10!
It is their best run since December 2021, when Carlo Ancelotti's side won 10 straight by defeating Atlético Madrid 2-0.
And Mbappé reached 75 Champions League goals!

Indeed. At 27 years and 339 days, he becomes the second-youngest player to reach 75 goals in the competition, behind only Lionel Messi at 27 years and 169 days. Ronaldo leads all-time with 140, Messi has 129, Lewandowski 109, and Benzema 90.
Look at Mbappé's underlying numbers from the match! Shots worth 1.72 non-penalty expected goals over 93 minutes, 12 progressive passes, and a match-high 0.36 expected threat!

Arda Güler was also crucial. Over his 69 minutes on the pitch, he created five chances for teammates, took 30 touches in the final third, and completed eight progressive passes. Bellingham created three chances in his 48 minutes alongside that stunning goal.
Off the pitch too, great news. Thibaut Courtois signed a massive new contract extension until summer 2028 and confirmed he wants to retire at Real Madrid!

He confirmed he feels very comfortable in Spain after returning from his knee injury. Technical Committee of Referees president Fran Soto also stated he wants to rebuild relations with Real Madrid following tensions surrounding refereeing and the Negreira scandal.
Right, over to cricket. What Vaibhav Sooryavanshi did against the UAE in Doha is just ridiculous!
The 15-year-old smashed a 53-ball 204 in the Rising Stars Asia Cup, breaking the world record for the fastest List A double century by reaching 200 off 52 balls.
He hit seven fours and 28 sixes! A strike rate of 384.90! Tilak said the match was done in the first five overs and called it absolute carnage.

India A chased down 250 in just 14.2 overs for a seven-wicket win. However, off-field conduct has raised concerns. Harbhajan Singh called the behaviour of both Indian and Pakistan players shameful following intense celebrations in the U-19 Asia Cup and India A's 48-run loss to Pakistan A, urging the ICC and boards to step in.
Padikkal has also made a compelling case for himself at number three in his last three Test outings.
Switching to Formula 1, Max Verstappen revealed he spent over 40 hours playing GTA VI in his hotel room during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend.
Forty hours! He was playing in the mornings and evenings between sessions and joked he completely forgot how to play Minecraft!
Looking ahead to Qatar, Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes have locked up the championships, but Red Bull leads McLaren by just nine points for third place in the constructors.
What about Toto Wolff on the Verstappen-Russell feud?

Wolff called their ongoing tension good entertainment, describing it as cat and mouse since their karting days. Russell had called Max a bully after Vegas, while Max declared Russell far below his level.
Over in tennis, Carlos Alcaraz has arrived in Bologna for the Davis Cup Finals Final 8 stage despite his left hamstring injury.
That comes right after winning the ATP Finals in Turin, where he defeated Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 to capture his 30th ATP title, equalling Jannik Sinner.
Andy Roddick was talking about Alcaraz's returns against Zverev on his podcast, saying Carlos controlled racket space like Novak Djokovic and gave him anxiety!
In the AFC Champions League Elite, Al Nassr defeated Al Sadd 2-1.
Cristiano Ronaldo scored a 13th-minute penalty, taking his career tally to 987 goals! Just 13 away from 1,000!
Mohammed Waad equalised for Al Sadd in the 22nd minute before getting sent off just before half-time. João Félix scored the winner with a 52nd-minute bicycle kick.
What else caught your eye?
Novak Djokovic filmed a cameo in the movie Focker-in-Law alongside Ben Stiller and Owen Wilson.
Brilliant!
For the Golden State Warriors, Brandon Williams is listed as questionable for Wednesday against Sacramento after missing time. He admitted watching the offense struggle was tough.
And Colton Herta will not join Cadillac in F1 for 2027, as they chose Valtteri Bottas to partner Sergio Perez despite Herta securing his 40 superlicence points.
Finally, Jannik Sinner underwent minor knee surgery in Turku, Finland for iliotibial band syndrome, putting his Australian Open participation at risk.
Around the grounds now. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed his century off just 28 balls against UAE, racing to 150 off 40!
That is incredible power hitting!
India A reached 108 inside six overs despite losing Abhishek Sharma for 12 and Prabhsimran Singh for three early on, chasing down 250 in 14.2 overs.

spoken: In European football, Real Madrid sit top of the Champions League power rankings after a matchday where Manchester City, Arsenal, Bayern Munich, and Paris Saint-Germain all failed to win.

While those clubs stumbled with injuries, our attack thrived. Florian Wirtz showed what he can do, and Jude Bellingham proved once again that he is one of the best midfielders in the world. Manchester United still refuse to have a normal day, but Real Madrid were top class.
The feeling around the squad has completely changed under Jose Mourinho. Even though Madrid are three points behind Barcelona in LaLiga, the squad is fully behind the Portuguese coach.

Bellingham put it perfectly when asked about his form. He just said, 'Mourinho, full stop.' He explained that Mourinho cares about how players are feeling, not just football. Look at the numbers: sixteen victories and two defeats in his first eighteen matches back. That is an eighty-eight point nine percent win rate, beating his first spell between 2010 and 2013.
They already have an eight-game winning streak, including a El Clasico win over Barcelona, plus comebacks in the Champions League against Roma and AEK Athens.
That relentless competitive spirit is back. And did you see what Rishabh Pant got up to in Christchurch on Wednesday?
He actually filled in for a local Last Man Stands team called Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park.

They were down a player in central Christchurch, asked Pant to join, and he picked up the bat! The man has hit one hundred and eight Test sixes in fifty-three matches, including six in Wellington during his 128 off 153 balls in that record 720 for nine total. What a way to keep his eye sharp before the second Test.

Speaking of that second Test, ball quality is still being debated. Shubman Gill raised concerns that Dukes and Kookaburra balls soften after twenty-five to thirty overs. New Zealand captain Tom Latham countered, saying pitch surfaces dictate wear and teams must simply adapt.

Over in Formula One, Max Verstappen took his seventy-fifth Grand Prix victory in Las Vegas without Gianpiero Lambiase on the radio for the first time since his debut Red Bull win in Spain back in 2016. Tom Hart stepped up as race engineer.

And off the track, the friction with George Russell continued. After their practice confrontation where Verstappen got a warning, Russell claimed someone had to stand up to him. F1 insider Will Buxton called Russell 'all mouth and no trousers'.

Max got the last laugh, winning the race while Russell hit the barriers trying to pass Kimi Antonelli for second with two laps left and ended up ninth. Now we head to Doha, but Max was very direct with De Telegraaf, saying he would rather stay at home given regional hostilities and missile risks, though he trusts the safety guarantees.
Remember, the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was cancelled and Sepang replaced Bahrain, where Verstappen won from pole, while Imola was stood down on 10 November.

In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz is in Bologna for Spain's Davis Cup quarter-final against Austria on Thursday. His hamstring is feeling a little better after picking up that injury against Daniil Medvedev last Wednesday, but he might be rested.
Alcaraz also spoke about Jannik Sinner's knee surgery, admitting that pushing to play every week is killing players and that everyone needs to learn from these scheduling mistakes.
Getting back to the NBA, that 129-110 win over the Kings was huge for Golden State. Steve Kerr saw the team bounce back after holding off the Kings rally to win that NorCal showdown.

They built on the momentum from snapping their five-game losing streak against Boston. And they did it shorthanded. Steph Curry remains out with a right oblique tear, Jimmy Butler III is recovering from ACL surgery, Moses Moody from patellar tendon surgery, and Kristaps Porzingis is away from the team.
Brandon Williams was questionable with a hamstring strain after giving an honest assessment of how tough the offense looks without Curry. Melton heating up from deep solved plenty of issues today.
How about Novak Djokovic joining Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller in a new Hollywood comedy?
The man has conquered tennis, so why not take on cinema?

On international football, Pep Guardiola spoke to Romario about Cristiano Ronaldo's situation with Portugal. Pep urged the federation to arrange a proper, dignified farewell, saying Ronaldo deserves a different ending and cannot leave the national team like this.
When Pep says a legend deserves a proper ending, the federation should listen.

In Formula One governance, the FIA finished an eight-month cost cap review for 2025. Williams committed an unintentional minor overspend breach and a procedural breach, while Alpine had a procedural breach. Nine teams and all five engine manufacturers complied fully.

And the drama at Ferrari keeps getting worse! Fred Vasseur had Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in his Sao Paulo hotel room after their lap one clash in Mexico City, where Leclerc went off at Turn 4 trying to pass outside and Verstappen took second place.

They left that meeting joking, but in Las Vegas, Leclerc tried to pass Hamilton at Turn 7, tipped his teammate into a spin, and got a ten-second penalty dropping him from sixth to tenth while Hamilton finished seventh. Vasseur asked Leclerc to see him before speaking to the media.

That garage must be tense. In tennis integrity, Arthur Rinderknech has been charged by the ITIA for allegedly refusing an anti-doping test in Brittany in June. He denies wrongdoing, faces a potential four-year ban, and is taking it to an Independent Tribunal with support from Marketa Vondrousova.
Also, Jannik Sinner confirmed minor right knee surgery, putting his Australian Open participation in serious doubt. The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July.

Around the grounds. Former England international Raheem Sterling received a twelve-month prison sentence, suspended for eighteen months, at Basingstoke Magistrates Court after pleading guilty to dangerous driving, possessing six nitrous oxide canisters, and failing to provide a specimen following a Lamborghini Urus crash on the M3 highway on 28 May. He was given a twenty-four month driving disqualification and one hundred hours of unpaid work.
Driving while inhaling balloons, incredible recklessness.
In the Champions League, Lille defeated Bayern Munich two-one.

spoken: Ten wins in a row across all competitions! We were trailing PSV 1-0 at the Bernabeu at half-time, looking sloppy just like against Celta Vigo. But Jose Mourinho made the right tweaks at the break!
Early passes behind their press changed everything. Jude Bellingham came off the bench for the second half, set up Vinicius Jr for our fifth goal, and bagged a wonderstrike.
Mbappe was sublime too! Two goals in the 64th and 84th minutes, plus the assist for Jude. Both made UEFA's Team of the Week, with Mbappe taking MVP. And how good has Arda Guler been?
Former Madrid midfielder Tote was on Radio MARCA saying Guler sees the game before everyone else. Four goals and nine assists in 16 matches speaks for itself.
Now, Christchurch! Day one of the second Test against New Zealand. Gurnoor Brar getting his Test cap from Jasprit Bumrah as player number 321—that was a special moment.
Bumrah told him to keep the cap with utmost respect. Brar delivered quickly, trapping Devon Conway lbw for 31 after Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to field.
Then Akash Deep tore through them! Three wickets in 22 balls for zero runs!

He adjusted his length fuller in the second session to make the batters play 90 percent of the time. KL Rahul dropped Tom Latham early off Akash, and Bumrah struggled to find his rhythm, but Akash kept India right in it.
Did you see Rishabh Pant playing local club cricket for Open House under the name 'Stan Stan'? Riding an electric bike in a purple tracksuit borrowing gear! Morne Morkel nearly fell off his chair!
Tom Latham called it brilliant character. Over in Formula 1, the feud between Max Verstappen and George Russell refuses to die down.

Max was brutally honest after Vegas. He called Russell an absolute joke this season and far below his level! Winning the race after George crashed out trying to overtake Antonelli made his day complete.
Russell tried to brush it off before Qatar, calling the drama amusing. But Jamie Chadwick noted that no driver gets under Max's skin quite like George.
On the court, Carlos Alcaraz has copied Pete Sampras! Lifting his left foot at the start of his service motion.
His coach Samuel Lopez explained the technical tweak. Alcaraz won 14 straight matches to take Vienna, Paris, and the ATP Finals, getting broken only three times in Turin.
And Carlos sent a heartfelt message to Jannik Sinner in Bologna after Sinner's right knee surgery, saying tennis misses him. They haven't met since April.
In tennis milestones, Alexander Zverev beat Arthur Fery in Germany's Davis Cup quarter-final against Great Britain in Bologna to reach 70 tour wins this year.
Joining Federer, Nadal, and Djokovic in that elite 70-win club in a single season! Huge achievement.
In the NBA, Sam Amick reported on Sactown Sports 1140 that Draymond Green is not untouchable in trade deadline talks for Golden State, with his expiring contract making trade numbers work easily.

Draymond on the trading block? That would mark a massive shift! In football, Carlos Tevez confirmed Lionel Messi will play in his testimonial at La Bombonera on December 20, and he wants Cristiano Ronaldo on the opposing team!
Imagine them sharing a pitch again. On the F1 grid, Haas confirmed Oliver Bearman for the 2027 season alongside rookie Rafael Camara, ending his frustration over contract delays.
And Fernando Alonso misses media day in Qatar with a viral infection contracted after Las Vegas, though Aston Martin expects him back in the car for Friday practice.
Around the grounds, Sunderland expressed disappointment after banned Jagiellonia Bialystok fans gained access to home areas at the Stadium of Light during their 1-1 Europa League draw.
UEFA had issued an away ban, but police and stewards had to step in during the opening minutes.
Also, former England scrum-half and legendary BBC Rugby Special presenter Nigel Starmer-Smith has died at the age of 81 following a battle with dementia.
